storedTranscript.text: Hello, James. I'm Ryota, and welcome to your English lesson! Today we'll talk about your work and the projects you're involved in, and practise two grammar points: the present perfect for experience, and the past simple for finished events. Does that sound good to you?
Oh, yes.

Great! Here is how the lesson goes. You'll answer some questions about your work, and then we'll practise the present perfect for your experience and the past simple for finished events. I'll also ask you follow-up questions to keep the conversation going, and I'll correct your mistakes, explain them, and give you a chance to try again. Near the end, you can practise your pronunciation if you like. First, there is a short level check, so I can adjust the lesson for you. Are you ready?
Oh, yes.

Wonderful. First, a short, friendly conversation. Please answer in English, and don't worry about mistakes. I just want to see what you can already do. Can you tell me a little about your job? What do you do?
I'm engineer.
Thank you. What kind of engineering do you do?
I make cars.
Cars, nice. Have you ever worked with an international customer? If so, can you tell me about it?
Uh, sorry.
No problem. Let me ask it more simply: have you ever worked with a customer from another country? (海外のお客さんと仕事をしたことはありますか。)
Uh, sorry. I don't understand.
Let me say it more simply. Have you ever worked with a customer from another country? 外国のお客さんと仕事をしたことはありますか。
Uh, please repeat.
Of course. Have you ever worked with a customer from another country?
Uh. next.
Okay, here is the last question. What is one thing you want to improve in your English?
Uh, time management.

ありがとうございます。時間管理は大切なテーマですね。では、仕事について英語で話す練習をしましょう。まず、基本の文を見てみましょう。

「I work in…」は「私は…で働いています」です。では、あなたの仕事について一文で言ってみてください。What do you do at work?
Uh, I
make car.

Good, you make cars. We say "I make cars," with an s on cars because there are many. Now try a full sentence with "I work in…", like the first example on the board.

Can you say "I work in…" and finish it with your company or department?
Uh, sorry. again?

もう一度言いますね。「I work in…」は「…で働いています」という意味です。

Now you say it. Start with "I work in" and add your department or the name of your team.
Uh, yes. For 7 year.

Seven years, good. We say "for seven years," with an s on years, because it is more than one year.

Please say the whole sentence, starting with "I have worked".
I have worked here for 7 years.

Yes, that's right. "I have worked here for seven years" is correct, because you started in the past and you still work here now.

Next is present perfect. Shall we go on, or do you have a question first?
Uh, yes.

現在完了は「have + 過去分詞」で、過去に始まって今も続いていることを表します。さっきの「I have worked here for seven years」がまさにその形です。

Have you worked for your current company for a long time? Answer with a full sentence that starts with "I have worked".
I work here for 7 years.

惜しいです。「I work here」は今の仕事を言う形です。「for seven years」と一緒に使うときは「I have worked」にします。

Try the sentence again, starting with "I have worked".
Uh, helps me build more cars.

車をもっと作るのに役立つ、ということですね。英語の勉強が仕事に役立つのは良いことです。では、さっきの文をもう一度、「I have worked」から始めて言ってみてください。

Does that make sense?
It has helped me build more cars.

Yes, "It has helped me build more cars" is correct. You used "has helped" for something that started in the past and still matters now.

Are you with me so far?
Uh, yes.
では、今度はひとりで答えてみてください。「I have worked」から始めて、今の会社で何年働いているか言ってみましょう。
Take your time. Start with "I have worked here for", and then add how many years you have worked at your company.
Yeah, quite a few. I actually attended maybe about six exhibitions throughout the year.
Next is past simple. Shall we go on, or do you have a question first?
Yes, I attended about six exhibitions last year.

Yes, that's right! "I attended about six exhibitions last year" is correct. "Last year" is a specific time in the past, so we use the past simple.

Now, a short one. When did you last meet a customer? Answer with a full sentence and a time word like "last week" or "two weeks ago".
Uh, Comdex in Los on Las Vegas was great. because it was very informative and very modern.

Comdex in Las Vegas sounds great! Your "it was great" and "it was very informative" are past simple, and they are correct. 過去のできごとを過去形で話せていますね。

What did you see there?
The future of technology and AI.

The future of technology and AI sounds very interesting. 「未来の技術とAI」ですね。

Have you ever used AI in your work? Answer with a full sentence that starts with "I have".
It definitely has. Um, I think less.
すみません、「I think less」はどういう意味でしょうか。仕事でAIを使ったことはありますか。Have you ever used AI at work? Please answer with "I have" if you can.
It's helped me be more efficient with my time.

Yes, that's right! "It has helped me be more efficient with my time" is correct. The help started in the past and it still continues now, so we use the present perfect.

Now, one more with "have". How long have you worked on your current project? Answer with "I have worked on…" and a time, like "for two years."
I worked on a project with a new car that can actually fly.

Good, a flying car is an interesting project! You said "I worked on", which is correct for a finished project. If the project is still going now, we say "I have worked on". Is the project still going?
Uh, yes, I did. There was about uh, 10 other engineers involved in the project.

Yes, you worked with about ten other engineers on that project. Because "engineers" is plural, we say "There were." 「複数形のときは were です。」

Can you say that sentence?
The largest or the biggest challenge was finding the technology allowing the car to lift off the ground.

Good sentence. "The biggest challenge was finding the technology" is clear and natural. 大変なところを具体的に説明できていますね。

How did you solve that problem?
The speed of change.
「The speed of change」は、技術の変化の速さのことですか。Did you mean that change was the challenge? Please tell me more, or say how you solved the problem.
Uh, move on.

わかりました、次に進みましょう。今度は、仕事で一番誇りに思っているプロジェクトについて話しましょう。

先ほどの空飛ぶ車のプロジェクトについて、もう少し教えてください。Try starting with "I worked on a project to…".

What is one project you are proud of? Tell me about it in two or three sentences, starting with "I worked on a project to…".
How much longer is this is this lesson?

About eight minutes are left. 残り約8分です。

We still have time for your project question, and then a short pronunciation practice and a summary. What is one project you are proud of? Start with "I worked on a project to…".
Please move on to pronunciation practice.

では、発音を練習しましょう。まず単語を一つ聞いて、後に続けて言ってください。

Listen, then repeat after me. Responsibilities.

Does that make sense so far?
Uh, just a little bit of individual words.

単語だけで練習しましょう。*responsibilities* の強い部分は、四つ目の音節です。re-spon-si-BIL-i-ties。もう一度、後に続けて言ってみてください。

Does that make sense?
I said individual words.

失礼しました。単語の練習はここで終わりにして、会話に戻りましょう。仕事で一番誇りに思っているプロジェクトを教えてください。

Try starting with "I worked on a project to…".

Are you with me so far?
Sorry, I have to finish now.

Of course, James. Today you used "I have worked here for seven years" and "I attended about six exhibitions last year" well, and you explained your flying-car project clearly. Next, practise "I have worked" for things that continue now, and "There were" with plural nouns. お疲れさまでした。また次回お会いしましょう。
